# matsindf

## Statement of need

Matrices are important mathematical objects, and they often describe
networks of flows among nodes. The power of matrices lies in their
ability to organize network-wide calculations, thereby simplifying the
work of analysts who study entire systems.

But [wouldn’t it be
nice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wouldn%27t_It_Be_Nice) if there were
an easy way to create `R` data frames whose entries were not numbers but
entire matrices? If that were possible, matrix algebra could be
performed on columns of similar matrices.

That’s the reason for `matsindf`. It provides functions to convert a
suitably-formatted
[tidy](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/articles/tidy-data.html) data frame
into a data frame containing a column of matrices.

Furthermore, `matsbyname` is a sister package that

- provides matrix algebra functions that respect names of matrix rows
  and columns (`dimnames` in `R`) to free the analyst from the task of
  aligning rows and columns of operands (matrices) passed to matrix
  algebra functions and
- allows matrix algebra to be conducted within data frames using
  [dplyr](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org),
  [tidyr](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org), and other
  [tidyverse](https://tidyverse.org) functions.

When used together, `matsindf` and `matsbyname` allow analysts to wield
simultaneously the power of both [matrix
mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_(mathematics)) and
[tidyverse](https://tidyverse.org) functional programming.

## Installation

You can install `matsindf` from CRAN with:

``` r
install.packages("matsindf")
```

You can install a recent development version of `matsindf` from github
with:

``` r
# install devtools if not already installed
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("MatthewHeun/matsindf")
# To build vignettes locally, use
devtools::install_github("MatthewHeun/matsindf", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

## History

The functions in this package were used in [Heun et al.
(2018)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2018.05.109).

## More Information

Find more information, including vignettes and function documentation,
at <https://MatthewHeun.github.io/matsindf/>.

## References

Heun, Matthew Kuperus, Anne Owen, and Paul E. Brockway. 2018. “A
Physical Supply-Use Table Framework for Energy Analysis on the Energy
Conversion Chain.” *Applied Energy* 226 (September): 1134–62.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2018.05.109>.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`UKEnergy2000`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/UKEnergy2000.md)
  : Energy consumption in the UK in 2000

- [`add_UKEnergy2000_matnames()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/add_UKEnergy2000_matnames.md)
  : Add a column of matrix names to tidy data frame

- [`add_UKEnergy2000_row_col_meta()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/add_UKEnergy2000_row_col_meta.md)
  : Add row, column, row type, and column type metadata

- [`build_keep_args()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/build_keep_args.md)
  : Build a list of arguments to keep

- [`build_matsindf_apply_data_frame()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/build_matsindf_apply_data_frame.md)
  : Create a data frame consisting of the input data for
  matsindf_apply()

- [`check_worksheet_name_violations()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/check_worksheet_name_violations.md)
  : Develop a warning message for malformed Excel worksheet names

- [`collapse_to_matrices()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/collapse_to_matrices.md)
  :

  Collapse a "tidy" data frame to matrices in a data frame (`matsindf`)

- [`df_to_msg()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/df_to_msg.md)
  : Create a message from a data frame

- [`everything_except()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/everything_except.md)
  : Get symbols for all columns except ...

- [`expand_to_tidy()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/expand_to_tidy.md)
  :

  Expand a `matsindf` data frame

- [`get_useable_default_args()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/get_useable_default_args.md)
  : Create a usable list of default arguments to a function

- [`group_by_everything_except()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/group_by_everything_except.md)
  : Group by all variables except some

- [`handle_empty_data()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/handle_empty_data.md)
  : Gracefully handle empty data

- [`handle_null_args()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/handle_null_args.md)
  :

  Gracefully handle `NULL` arguments

- [`index_column()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/index_column.md)
  : Index a column in a data frame by groups relative to an initial year

- [`mat_to_rowcolval()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/mat_to_rowcolval.md)
  : Convert a matrix to a data frame with rows, columns, and values.

- [`matrix_cols()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/matrix_cols.md)
  : Find columns that contain matrices

- [`matsindf_apply()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/matsindf_apply.md)
  :

  Apply a function to a `matsindf` data frame (and more)

- [`matsindf_apply_types()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/matsindf_apply_types.md)
  :

  Determine types of `.dat` and `...` arguments for matsindf_apply()

- [`rowcolval_to_mat()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/rowcolval_to_mat.md)
  : Collapse a tidy data frame into a matrix with named rows and columns

- [`should_unlist()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/should_unlist.md)
  : Tell whether a column can be unlisted

- [`verify_cols_missing()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/verify_cols_missing.md)
  : Verify that column names in a data frame are not already present

- [`where_to_get_args()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/where_to_get_args.md)
  : Decide where to get each argument to FUN

- [`write_mats_to_excel()`](https://matthewheun.github.io/matsindf/reference/write_mats_to_excel.md)
  : Write matrices to an Excel file
